newsitem.title: UK: Two feared dead in ship mutiny off West Africa.
newsitem.headline: Two feared dead in ship mutiny off West Africa.

text.p: Two people were missing and feared dead after a mutiny by two crew members on a ship in the Gulf of Guinea off the West African coast, Lloyd's shipping service said on Wednesday.
Lloyd's, quoting coastguard personnel, said the mutineers on the 4,455 gross ton MV Janna had eventually been overpowered and locked up.
The ship, which was thought to have a crew of nine, was travelling from Nigeria's Port Harcourt to Takoradi in Ghana when it issued a distress signal late on Tuesday.
Lloyd's said the ship's master and chief engineer were missing and believed dead. The remainder of the crew locked themselves in the wheelhouse and bridge for safety.
"The two crew (mutineers) were eventually overpowered and are now locked up," said Lloyd's.
The ship was owned by a German company and registered in Antigua and Barbuda.
No other details were immediately available.
